purpose: Break up the conspicuously smooth first-kilometre launch scarps while preserving the Copernicus terrain, shoreline, route, collision, and solver authorities.

dry_scarp_outcrops.asset_source: existing rights-reviewed CC0 Rock Moss Set 01 six-variant project kit
dry_scarp_outcrops.route_clearance: outside active channel and full-route clearance gate
dry_scarp_outcrops.authority: procedural presentation only; no Batoka lithology, geospatial, collision, hydraulic, raft-force, navigation, or rapid-line authority

rejected_brackets.reason: Technically valid but mostly occluded by the 2.5 m adaptive launch overlay and visually too subtle at gameplay distance.
Produced floating silhouettes, oversized boulders, and severe black shadow wedges; not versioned.
Removed the giant forms but retained long low-sun shadow wedges; superseded by the non-shadow-casting retained layer.

findings: Sparse grounded forms now interrupt parts of the skyline and upper dry scarps without the rejected black shadow wedges.
The conditioned shoreline remains continuous and no outcrop enters the water or active route in the retained frame.
The dominant left wall still reads broad, bright, and smooth; the change is incremental rather than a photoreal promotion.
The water, raft, characters, and procedural vegetation remain visibly synthetic in this frame.

verification.editor_build: SmokeEmIfYouGotEmEditor Mac Development succeeded after the retained source changes

open_external_acceptance_gates: A named whitewater water-VFX and environment-art reviewer must approve the foam, crest, hole, spray, mist, reflection, transmission, shoreline-contact, terrain, and ecology presentation across representative flow bands.
Qualified guides for the represented rivers must approve rapid identity, aeration placement, line and hazard readability, and raft/swimmer occlusion at the represented flows.
A geospatial or technical-art reviewer must approve source alignment and the labeled procedural terrain, bank, bathymetry, rapid-geometry, and dry-scarp outcrop infill boundaries.
A rights and provenance reviewer must approve every production texture, mesh, reference-media use, attribution, and redistribution record.

A safety and gameplay-readability reviewer must approve that foam, spray, mist, vegetation, lighting, terrain dressing, raft, and characters do not hide hazards, swimmers, rescue targets, or solver failures.
Target-platform qualification must pass desktop performance, memory, streaming, fresh-machine rendering, and required VR or low-power readability budgets.
The product owner must approve the integrated moving-camera river, raft, equipment, character, animation, and water interaction presentation before M9 or photoreal promotion.
